Thought: I need to determine which characteristic remains unchanged between two polymorphs of a compound. Let me analyze each option:

A. Physical attributes like melting points - Polymorphs typically have different physical properties including melting points, so this would change.

B. The nature of intermolecular interactions - Polymorphs have different crystal structures due to different intermolecular interactions, so this would change.

C. The chemical formulae - Polymorphs are different crystalline forms of the same chemical compound, so they must have identical chemical formulae.

D. Torsional angles - Polymorphs often have different molecular conformations, which would include different torsional angles.

Since polymorphs are different crystalline forms of the same chemical compound, they must have the same chemical composition (formula) but differ in their crystal structure, physical properties, and molecular arrangements.
Final Answer: Polymorphs are different crystalline forms of the same chemical compound. By definition, they have identical chemical compositions but differ in their crystal structures and physical properties.
